## Why this note exists

The introduction figure @fig-reach-products (`figures/fig02-reach-products.png`,
built by `R/fct_reach_products.R`) breaks Norwegian declared copper down by
**use category** (`anvendelseskategori`). This note records what that
classification actually is, where it is documented, and how much each category
matters for copper *in the environment* -- because the tonnage ranking in the
figure is a poor proxy for that.

## The classification: Use Categories Nordic (UCN)

- The `anvendelseskategori` codes in Produktregisteret are **UCN -- Use
  Categories Nordic**.
- Norway, Sweden and Denmark **harmonised** their product-register use
  categories into UCN in **2002**. Finland kept the EU use-category system.
- UCN is not a REACH artefact. It predates the harmonised REACH use-descriptor
  system (Chapter R.12), and is rooted in the earlier Nordic product-register
  practice. So it is a *cousin* of the REACH PC list, not a copy (see below).

## Where it is written down

| Resource | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| **SPIN** database guide, section 3.1.3 -- `spin2000.net` (older) / `spin2020.com` | The UCN code list and per-category definitions. SPIN (*Substances in Preparations / Products in Nordic Countries*) is the public front end to all four Nordic product registers. |
| **KEMI** (Swedish Chemicals Agency), "About the Products Register" | The same codes, documented on the Swedish side. |
| **Miljodirektoratet** -- Produktregisteret + `deklareringsforskriften` (FOR-2015-05-19-541) | Who runs the register, the declaration obligation (declared chemicals, >= 100 kg/yr), and the declaration guidance. |

The SPIN site was intermittently unreachable when this note was written
(2026-09); the section reference (3.1.3) and the KEMI page are the stable
pointers.

## UCN already encodes environmental relevance

This is the useful part. UCN is **not just descriptive** -- SPIN assigns, per
use category:

- an **emission potential** by compartment (soil / water / air);
- a **Use Index** and a **Use Exposure Number** (the latter weighted by, e.g.,
  the volatile fraction of the substances declared under that category, which
  raises the exposure number to air).

SPIN's own worked example: *"the use category 'herbicides' indicates a high
emission potential to soil, while 'biocidal products for human use' points to a
high human exposure."*

The REACH-world equivalent is the **ERC -- Environmental Release Category** in
ECHA Guidance R.12: each use gets an ERC encoding wide-dispersive vs
industrial-contained, and indoor vs outdoor.

## Our eight lumped categories, ranked by what matters

`reach_product_summary()` keeps the seven largest categories by declared net
quantity and pools the rest as "Other". Ordered instead by **environmental
relevance**:

| Lumped category | ~ECHA R.12 PC | Release pattern | Environmental relevance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Insecticides & other plant pest control agents | PC27 | applied to fields/crops; deliberate outdoor dispersion (ERC 8d/8f) | **high** |
| Biocides | PC8 | antifoulants, wood preservatives, disinfectants -> water / soil (ERC 8a-8f) | **high** |
| Fertilisers, general | PC12 | spread on land; Cu as a micronutrient additive -> soil (ERC 8e/8f) | **high** |
| Drilling chemicals incl. crude oil/gas | (no clean PC; ~PC40) | offshore; produced-water and cuttings discharge to sea | **high, marine-specific** |
| Process control agents (pH-regulators, flocculants, precipitants) | PC20 | often water-treatment-adjacent; partial release to water (ERC 8a/8b) | medium |
| Absorption and adsorption materials | PC2 | release mostly at end-of-life (spent adsorbent disposal) | low-medium |
| Synthesis raw materials and intermediates | PC19 | consumed in further synthesis inside industrial installations; contained (ERC 6a) | **low** |
| Other | mixed | paint, coatings, cleaning agents are dispersive; surface treatment, printing inks, polishes less so | mixed |

## The headline

**Tonnage is not environmental relevance.** "Synthesis raw materials and
intermediates" is the single largest declared category (~40,000 t/yr net) but is
a **contained industrial use** (PC19 / ERC 6a): the copper is consumed making
another substance, with minimal environmental release. The uses that actually
put copper *into* the Norwegian environment are the dispersive ones --
**biocides, plant-protection products, fertilisers, and offshore drilling
chemicals** -- which sit lower down the tonnage ranking.

Consequence for the paper: if @fig-reach-products is used to argue "where does
Norway's copper go", it needs that caveat in the text, or panel (a) should be
ordered / annotated by release potential rather than (or alongside) tonnage. The
tier column above is a first pass; it could become an `emission_tier` column on
`reach_product_category_translations()` in `R/fct_reach_products.R`.

## Data provenance

- Source file: `inst/extdata/emissions/REACH_copper_prtd.xlsx`, sheet
  `kobber sum på produkttype`.
- Obtained from Miljodirektoratet by personal communication, **2 May 2025**
  (correspondence quoted in `docs/NBXX-REACH.qmd`).
- "Net quantity" = imported + produced - exported, per declaration. Declared
  (`deklareringspliktige`) chemicals only, >= 100 kg/yr.
- Reporting years **2018--2023**.
- Norwegian -> English translation and the top-7-plus-"Other" lumping:
  `reach_product_category_translations()` and `reach_product_lumped()` in
  `R/fct_reach_products.R`.

## The full translation table

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ucn-translations
suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(quiet = TRUE))
reach_product_category_translations() |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$category_en) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Register category (Norwegian)", "English", "Confidence", "Note"
    )
  )
```
